title: Revision guards are workspace-wide: an unrelated task edit invalidates a captured revision for a task that never changed
description:
External report from the mbpm2 project, relayed by opum-agent 2026-09-15 18:50Z, listed among missing capabilities and described as the most concrete of them. REPRODUCED first-hand on quest 0.7.1 -- the report is accurate, and this task exists to record the measurement rather than the claim.

REPRODUCTION, in a disposable workspace with two unrelated tasks T-1 and T-2:
  capture T-1 revision via `quest task view T-1 --json` -> 6ab6e565...
  `quest task edit T-2 --add-note ...`                  -> exit 0   (T-2 only)
  `quest task edit T-1 --if-revision <T-1 revision>`    -> exit 5   CONFLICT
T-1 was never written to between the capture and the guarded edit. Editing an unrelated record invalidated it. The guard itself works correctly in the per-task sense too -- re-using an genuinely stale T-1 revision after T-1 moves also returns exit 5 -- so the mechanism is sound and only its SCOPE is wrong.

WHY IT MATTERS TO THE REPORTER: they run concurrent research sessions against one workspace. Workspace-wide scope means any two sessions writing different tasks conflict, so --if-revision is unusable as a safety mechanism precisely in the case it was built for. Its documented purpose (help text for task edit, QCLI-277) is stated in per-record terms -- "capture revision from an earlier task view --json, and the edit is refused ... if THE RECORD has moved since" -- so the implemented scope also contradicts the documentation.

ACCEPTANCE EXAMPLE, their shape: the sequence above returns exit 0 on the final command, because T-1 did not move. Exit 5 remains correct when T-1 itself has moved.

THE OTHER REPORTED GAPS -- field selection, note cursors, individual-note reads, zero-note projections -- are not reproduced here and are recorded on this task only as context. They should be separated into their own tasks if taken up; they are read-shaping conveniences, whereas this one is a correctness gap against the documented contract.

CONFIRMED WORKING in the same external report, evidence worth keeping because it is not otherwise available: an expanded 111-test suite with zero skips including real CLI integration tests, quest note limits, stale-write guards, typed proof relations, dependency traversal, version-drift warnings, and preservation of claim metadata. Their qualification tasks CON-52/53/54 are Done. Full report at results/analysis/proof-graph-pilot-20260913/build-validation/lore-0.7.0-quest-0.7.1-20260915/validation-report.md on their side.

acceptanceCriteria.text: --if-revision is scoped to the record being written: editing an unrelated task does not invalidate a captured revision, demonstrated by the two-task reproduction returning exit 0 on the final command
Exit 5 is still returned when the guarded record itself has moved since the revision was captured, proven as a separate run rather than inferred from the first
The help text for task edit and the workspace docs agree with the implemented scope, since they currently describe per-record behavior that the implementation does not provide
The reporter is told the result either way, including if the workspace-wide scope turns out to be load-bearing for something and cannot narrow

plan: 1. Capture the four pre-fix controls on the published 0.11.0 (unrelated edit -> exit 5 on task edit and on a batch item; guarded record moved -> exit 5 in both; the last two must SURVIVE the fix as exit 5).
2. Sweep every consumer of the public revision value across the fleet, two passes (bare field name, then command invocation), and characterise the pattern searched.

3. Narrow the capture value and both guards to the record: task view emits a per-record revision; task edit --if-revision and task edit-batch per-item ifRevision compare against that record own revision; the internal workspace CAS and edit-batch data.revision stay workspace-scoped and untouched.
4. Update the help text and the tests, adding the two-task reproduction as a regression test alongside the existing same-record cases.
5. Run bun run check, then verify on CI via the PR source-gates run rather than trusting a local-only result (DEC-17).
6. Branch, PR, merge to dev; report the outcome to opum-agent and tell the reporter either way (AC4).
implementationNotes:
IMPLEMENTATION NOTE, 2026-09-29. Reproduced first-hand on the published 0.11.0 BEFORE changing anything, with the pre-fix controls captured in the same disposable workspace: two tasks T-1/T-2, editing T-2 moved T-1's viewed revision from 919404e5... to fcb5477b..., and the guarded edit of T-1 then exited 5. Editing the guarded record ITSELF also exited 5, and a `task edit-batch` item whose own record moved failed as well. So the mechanism is sound and only its SCOPE is wrong, exactly as the external report says.

ROOT CAUSE: `src/application/tasks/local-task-repository.ts` `revision()` hashes `JSON.stringify(snapshot)`, and `snapshot` is the whole workspace (`taskRecords` + `drafts`). `viewWithRevision` emitted that value and `editOn` compared against it, so both ends were self-consistent but workspace-scoped -- which is why the guard looked correct in every same-record test.

FIX: a record-scoped revision (sha256 over one record's `{task, location}`) in the new `src/application/tasks/record-revision.ts`; `task view` emits it; the `editOn` guard, the CLI's QCLI-374 pre-fold check, and `editBatch`'s per-item guard all compare against it. `location` is in the hash because `task view` reports the derived `path` beside the record, so a relocation must move the revision too. Deliberately NOT narrowed: the repository's internal `expectedRevision` CAS (still workspace-wide, still under the write lock) and `edit-batch`'s reported `data.revision` (still the workspace revision the batch committed at, pinned since QCLI-122).

PROOF PAIR, both halves run in this session. With `src/` reverted to pre-fix and only the new tests kept, `test/cli-task-edit-if-revision.test.ts` is 3 fail / 7 pass; with the fix it is 10 pass / 0 fail. The three that fail pre-fix are the AC1 reproduction, the AC2 control row, and the new batch row. The pre-existing same-record staleness rows AND the QCLI-374 by-value removal rows pass in BOTH states -- that is what makes them the must-not-regress controls rather than evidence for the fix.

CONSUMER SWEEP, two passes, every sibling checkout under /Volumes/external/repos, tracked files only: pass 1 matched the bare field name (`revision`, cross-filtered to the quest context), pass 2 matched the command invocation (`quest task view` / `task edit` / `task edit-batch`, including assembled argv arrays). ONE production consumer: lore-cli. It reads `task view`'s revision into `detail.revision` (`src/adapters/quest.ts`) and sends it as `--if-revision` from `guardedEditTask` (`src/commands/link.ts`), so the documented capture-then-supply flow is preserved and improved. The sweep found NO repository that sets `edit-batch`'s per-item `ifRevision`, so that narrowing has no consumer at all; `opum-cli-e2e` reads `edit-batch`'s `data.revision` only to interpolate a progress string (their own CLAUDE.md calls it cosmetic) and that value is unchanged.

THE ONE REAL CONSEQUENCE, verified at the source rather than taken from the sweep report: lore-cli's `src/commands/link.ts` states the old scope in a comment ("WORKSPACE-WIDE (measured on 0.10.0 and 0.11.0)") and `test/link-quest-race.test.ts` carries a positive control asserting that T-1's viewed revision moved under a T-2 write. Both describe the previous implementation and need updating when lore-cli picks this up. Their decision logic does not depend on the scope -- they already decline to decide on revision movement alone -- so the narrower hash strengthens that choice. Reported to opum-agent for routing.
finalSummary:
Fixed in opum-ai/quest-cli#415 (head 3c5afb15; source-gates push run 36528753986 and pull_request run 36528760436, Tracker integrity 36528760473, lore check 36528760458 -- all success on that SHA).

`--if-revision` was workspace-scoped at BOTH ends: `task view --json` emitted a sha256 of the entire store (every task record and every draft) and the guard compared against that same value, so writing any task invalidated every other record's captured revision and a guarded edit of a record that never moved was refused with exit 5. Reproduced first-hand on published 0.11.0 before the change, and re-measured after: T-1 is byte-identical after T-2 is written, the guarded edit returns exit 0, and it still returns exit 5 once T-1 itself moves.

The revision is now a pure function of the located record (`src/application/tasks/record-revision.ts`), so capture (`task view`) and check (`editOn`, `editBatch` per item, and the CLI's QCLI-374 pre-fold guard) are the same function of the same bytes and cannot drift. Deliberately unchanged: the repository's internal `expectedRevision` CAS (INV-3) and `edit-batch`'s reported `data.revision` (pinned since QCLI-122).

Proof pair, both halves run: src reverted with the new tests kept = 3 fail / 7 pass; fixed = 10 pass / 0 fail. Full `bun run check` on the final tree: 989 pass / 0 fail. Consumer sweep found lore-cli the only production consumer, whose capture-then-supply flow is preserved and improved; its `link.ts` comment and `link-quest-race.test.ts` positive control describe the old scope and were reported to opum-agent.
